MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  MARCH 1, 2023
  TELECONFERENCED  VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  5:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Frost called the meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Chris Frost; Commissioners Daphne Anneet, Keegan Gibbs, and Brian
  Merrick; and Ex Officio Member Brent Woodworth

  ABSENT:  Vice Chair Joshua Spiegel

  ALSO PRESENT:  Susan Duenas, Public Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works
  Director; Luis Flores, Public Safety Liaison; Gabe Etcheverry, Fire Safety Liaison; Jerry
  Vandermeulen, Fire Safety Liaison; Arthur Aladjadjian, Public Works Superintendent;
  Parker Davis, Media Technician; Lieutenant Dustin Carr, Los Angeles County Sheriff's
  Department; and Mary Linden, Executive Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Chair Frost moved, and Commissioner Merrick seconded a motion to approve the
  agenda with Item Nos. 2.B. and 2.C. to be heard after Item No. 5.B. The question
  was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Vice Chair Spiegel absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Executive Assistant Linden reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on February 24, 2023

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/ PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Lloyd Ahern was not present.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Chair Frost moved, and Commissioner Gibbs seconded a motion to approve the
  Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Vice Chair
  Spiegel absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes February 1, 2023
  —

  Staff recommendation: Approve minutes of the Public Safety Commission
  Regular meeting of February 1, 2023.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS (continued)

  Megan Whitcomb discussed funding for a speed bump by Sycamore School in Las
  Flores Canyon due to speeding on the road. She asked if the school could provide
  funding for signs until the City could discuss it during its regular budget process.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Point Dume Headlands
  Recommended Action: 1) Review public safety concerns in the Point Dume
  headlands area; and 2) Identify potential solutions to be executed in coordination
  with the Sheriff’s Department, Volunteers on Patrol (VOP), and California State
  Parks (State Parks).

  Public Safety Director Dueflas presented the report. She introduced California State
  Parks Chief Ranger Darrell Readyhoff.

  Steve Graham stated he lived in the area and was greatly impacted by the parking
  situation. He stated this serious safety concern got incrementally worse every week.
  He stated he spoke often with VOP and Sheriff’s Department (LASD) personnel,
  and he commended them for wanting to help find a positive solution. He stated
  many cars illegally or unsafely parked immediately after the first vehicle did so. He
  discussed vehicles using Cliffside Drive as a drag strip.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of March 1, 2023
Page 3 of 9

  Chair Frost agreed with Mr. Graham. He stated he personally observed a car park
  on Mr. Graham’s yard. He stated some of the drivers were not open to discussing
  problems with how they were parking.

  Commissioner Merrick stated he provided written comments about his concerns.
  He stated he lived around the corner from the area. He commended the VOP for
  writing tickets. He stated there was no State Parks presence. He noted that VOP
  could not tow vehicles. He stated State Parks listed Cliffside Drive as the entrance
  to Point Dume State Park. He suggested signage directing vehicles to park at Point
  Dume State Beach. He suggested the City contact Trip Advisor or other apps to
  cooperate with not listing the headlands address as Cliffside Drive. He stated State
  Parks rangers usually arrived in the early morning when there was little or no traffic.
  He suggested they come in the afternoon or at sunset when there were more visitors.
  He stated the City needed to figure out who can tow vehicles. He suggested the City
  consider hiring a dedicated tow enforcement vehicle. He suggested LASD and State
  Parks improve their coordination. He expressed concern for the state of the park as
  well.

  Mark Russo, VOP, stated they had been watching the area for a while, He stated
  the number of visitors was often weather driven. He stated VOP patrol was
  dedicated to the area Saturday through Monday on Presidents Day weekend. He
  stated many visitors were coming for the first time, and many were driven by social
  media. He stated existing signage indicated where parking was not allowed but not
  where parking was permitted. He stated VOP issued many citations, answered
  questions about where to park, and assisted handicapped individuals safely get to
  the headlands. He agreed signage was needed to direct motorists to where they
  should park. He stated visitors should be educated on social media. He stated
  enforcement was needed there every weekend, including after sunset when parking
  was restricted.

  In response to Commissioner Merrick, Chair Frost stated State Parks rangers could
  cite and tow. He discussed how illegal parking blocked ADA access on the
  decomposed granite (DG) pathways.

  Commissioner Merrick stated State Parks was supposed to have a dedicated ranger
  there but never has.

  Mr. Russo suggested posts be installed to deter parking on the walkways.

  Chief Ranger Readyhoff discussed his work in Malibu since 1999. He stated State
  Parks had a three-prong approach for the headlands, including ranger patrols,
  parking enforcement employees, and ambassadors providing information. He stated
  park employees were there to provide information and assist visitors. He stated
  State Parks issued 506 parking citations in that area in 2022 and 99 so far this year.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of March 1, 2023
Page 4 of 9

  He stated he would make this area a priority, especially at sunset hours. He
  confirmed that ranger and lifeguard peace officers could tow vehicles for blocking
  the road. He stated three rangers patrolled from Point Mugu to the Malibu Pier and
  Malibu Creek State Park. He announced two new peace officers were starting soon
  along with more parking enforcement officials. He stated citations would not stop
  people from coming.

  In response to Chair Frost, Chief Ranger Readyhoff discussed enforcement of ADA
  accessibility. In response to Chief Ranger Readyhoff, Commissioner Merrick
  confirmed the City owned the walkway.

  Chair Frost stated there was a problem with dogs and drones in the park. In response
  to Chair Frost, Chief Ranger Readyhoff confirmed drones were prohibited by State
  Parks.

  Commissioner Merrick displayed a photo of pedestrians walking around cars
  parked on the pathway. Chief Ranger Readyhoff stated all those cars were towable.

  In response to Chief Ranger Readyhoff, Mr. Russo stated there was only one tow
  company in Malibu. He stated response time was a problem.

  Chair Frost stated Public Safety Director Dueñas was working on an agreement for
  a temporary tow yard this summer at the high school.

  Commissioner Merrick asked if State Parks could perform a census of who and how
  many were visiting each of its parks in Malibu.

  Chief Ranger Readyhoff and Commissioner Merrick discussed the history of State
  Parks, City of Malibu, and Coastal Commission in this area.

  Commissioner Anneet stated she lived in that area for many years. She stated it was
  now a public safety crisis and state of emergency. She said what had been done
  until now was not adequate. She stated State Parks promoted public access to the
  bluffs even though it is a nature preserve. She stated protecting the sidewalk was a
  top priority. She stated Lot 22 protected residents parking on Westward Beach
  Road. She agreed with Commissioner Merrick about the need for signage. She
  questioned who had jurisdiction to post signs directing people where to park. She
  thanked Chief Ranger Readyhoff for his attendance. She suggested State Parks
  increase its enforcement and citations. She expressed concern for Mr. Graham and
  his family. She asked who would take action and how quickly.

  Chair Frost asked if Public Works could add split railing by the DG pathway. Public
  Works Director DuBoux stated finding would take time. He stated he could add
  this to the five-year capital improvements project (CIP) list and make it a priority
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of March 1, 2023
Page 5 of 9

  for next year. He stated he would look into whether the City could put down
  delineators as a temporary, interim safety measure.

  Commissioner Merrick suggested installing bollards instead of split rail. Public
  Works Director DuBoux agreed and stated he would develop some options.

  Commissioner Anneet stated some residents may complain about the eyesore, but
  it was more important to address the public safety emergency. Public Works
  Director DuBoux stated the delineators were easily removed, if necessary.

  Chair Frost stated educating the public of the reason for the measures was
  important. He stated split rail had a rural feel.

  Commissioner Anneet stated wooden posts like those installed in Lot 22 would be
  more acceptable.

  In response to Commissioner Anneet, Mr. Graham discussed a resident who parked
  a golf cart. He stated the problem with bollards was at the corner of Birdview and
  Cliffside due to illegal parking and unsafe departures from those parking spots. He
  stated anything rural would be best, but he thought no Point Dume residents would
  complain because they were all aware of the problem. He thanked everyone for
  trying to find a solution.

  In response to Commissioner Anneet, Chair Frost stated responsibility for signage
  would depend on in which agency’s jurisdiction the signs were placed.

  Chief Ranger Readyhoff discussed State Parks signage. He stated it was at the main
  entrance and directed them to the beach lot for additional parking.

  Commissioner Merrick stated he worked with Lindsay Templeton at State Parks to
  get the signs currently installed. He suggested signage was needed at the entry of
  Birdview.

  Commissioner Anneet suggested adding signage at the entrances to Point Dume to
  direct motorists to Westward Beach Road to get to the headlands. Chief Ranger
  Readyhoff stated he through that property was owned either by the City, Los
  Angeles County Department of Beaches and Harbors (Beaches and Harbors), or
  private landowners.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated the City could issue an encroachment permit
  to State Parks. He stated it would be best for State Parks to place the signs.

  Commissioner Anneet stated the intersection of Cliffside and Birdview was listed
  on the State Parks website as the location of and access to the headlands. She
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of March 1, 2023
Page 6 of 9

  requested that address be changed. Chief Ranger Readyhoff stated he would see if
  that could be changed.

  Mr. Russo stated the majority of traffic was coming off Dume Drive and Cliffside
  Drive over Presidents Day weekend. He stated it could be that directional apps were
  sending them that way. He discussed restricted parking on streets in that area. He
  stated vehicles often lined up at the entrance to the headlands waiting for a spot to
  open. He suggested adding a sign stating “no waiting for parking” with directions
  to additional parking.

  Chair Frost requested Chief Ranger Readyhoff come back to the Commission with
  an update.

MOTION  Chair Frost moved, and Commissioner Gibbs seconded a motion to continue the
  item to a future meeting for further discussion.

  Commissioner Gibbs stated the City often made deals with other agencies that were
  not followed up on. He asked how the City could hold them accountable. He asked
  who at the City would be responsible for monitoring it.

  Public Safety Director Dueñas suggested that could be discussed when the item
  came back. She suggested inviting the same representatives to attend the next
  meeting.

  Chair Frost agreed with Commissioner Gibbs that someone needed to follow up.

  Commissioner Anneet asked which agreements had been executed in the past.

  Chief Ranger Readyhoff stated the Point Dume Natural Preserve website indicated
  it began at the cul de sac. He stated the website indicated disabled parking was
  available on Cliffside Drive with other parking down below. In response to Chief
  Ranger Readyhoff, Commissioner Anneet stated it might be third party sites
  showing the local streets.

  Commissioner Gibbs suggested asking the City Attorney if the City had an avenue
  to pressure partner agencies to hold up their end of agreements. He discussed the
  problem with handshake agreements.

  The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Vice Chair Spiegel absent.

  Chair Frost discussed a No Parking / Tow Away sign that was recently removed
  and tossed across the street.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of March 1, 2023
Page 7 of 9

  Ryan Embree asked the hours that visitors could be at the Nature Preserve. He
  stated defining lanes with an edge strip would make ticketing easier. He stated the
  nuisance was created by patronage of the property. He stated tightening up access
  was the answer. He requested staff report a history of other problems and crime
  when this item was brought back. He suggested a camera be installed to monitor
  the area remotely and respond. He suggested very short, reflective candlesticks or
  many Botts dots be used.

  Lieutenant Carr commended everyone for the excellent ideas presented. He stated
  his research showed only three calls for LASD response to illegal parking so far
  this year. He suggested designating 18 parking spots at Point Dume for handicap
  parking only. He agreed with using bollards for a more natural look. He stated a
  shared car and bike lane could be considered. He stated LASD could not tow
  vehicles parked on private property, but owners could call a tow truck to remove
  the vehicles at owner expense. He agreed the residents have legitimate concerns.

  At 6:10 p.m., Commissioner Merrick left the meeting.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS (continued)

  B.  Public Safety Agency Activity
  Recommended Action: Discuss recent Public Safety Agency activities and
  receive and file activity reports from the County of Los Angeles Sheriffs
  Department, Fire Department, and Lifeguard Division.

  Lieutenant Carr stated the LASD survey of recreational vehicles (RV5) on
  PCH this week showed seven in mid-afternoon. He discussed trends in
  citations for oversized vehicles. He stated he toured the substation at the
  new SMC campus. He stated it was on schedule. He discussed traffic and
  crime trends. He announced Malibu Canyon Road was currently closed
  from Civic Center Way to Piuma Road for at least 12 hours due to a
  landslide.

ITEM 2.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Safety Director Dueñas stated a reporter from The Malibu Times posted
  video of the rockslide on Malibu Canyon Road. She announced Jerry
  Vandermeulen had returned to the City as a Fire Safety Liaison. She stated three
  dedicated interim homeless beds were now being filled by The People Concern
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of March 1, 2023
Page 8 of 9

  (TPC) Outreach Team. She stated the first automatic license plate reader (ALPR)
  camera was up and being hardwired.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores stated other ALPR cameras were being explored with
  SCE and Caltrans for possible encroachment permits. He stated the Outreach Team
  moved eight individuals off the street in January, with four placed in interim
  housing or shelter, one in permanent housing, and three reunited with their families.
  He stated he was working with the school district on paperwork for the temporary
  impound yard at the high school from Memorial Day to Labor Day.

  Chair Frost welcomed Fire Safety Liaison Vandermeulen back to the City. He
  commended the Fire Safety Liaison team.

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry stated they were ecstatic to have Fire Safety Liaison
  Vandermeulen back. He stated it was determined that Los Angeles County Forestry
  had been responsible for brush clearance signs but was no longer supporting that
  program. He stated the City agreed to fund 12 new signs that have been installed.
  He stated eight Beacon Boxes were received and ready to be installed. He stated
  the City requested the remaining 17 be shipped all at once. He stated beacon lights
  on the Beacon Boxes were not working and the vendor had agreed to remedy that.
  He stated the hazard tree removal grant was moving ahead. He requested
  Commissioners or residents report any trees that may be eligible for removal.

  In response to Chair Frost, Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry explained the lights on
  the Beacon Boxes had solar panels and came on in the dark.

  Public Works Director DuBoux discussed rockslides on Malibu Canyon and on
  PCH at the city limits. He discussed safety issues near the Caltrans Trancas Bridge
  project. He stated the pavement was being repaired and striping refreshed, weather
  permitting. He stated the new section on the bridge should be done by April. He
  commended the City’s road crews for prompt and thorough storm response and
  cleanup. He stated another storm was expected in one week to nine days.

  Chair Frost commended City staff and road crews for their great work.

ITEM 2.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth announced Anthony Maffone had been named Los
  Angeles County Fire Chief by the Board of Supervisors. He stated that should help
  get community brigade memorandum of understanding (MOU) signed sooner. He
  discussed a Chamber of Commerce meeting covering safety and community
  support for preparedness. He discussed being in Washington, DC for pending bill
  HR 176 that would help Woolsey Fire victims get tax relief for settlement funds
  received.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of March 1, 2023
Page 9 of 9

  In response to Ex Officio Member Woodworth, Public Works Director DuBoux
  stated an update on the Caltrans plan for PCH intersections at Las Flores Canyon
  Road and Rambla Pacifico would be discussed in an upcoming coordination
  meeting with Caltrans. He stated the City’s project for that intersection was
  scheduled for the next fiscal year.

  In response to Ms. Whitcomb, Ex Officio Member Woodworth stated he agreed
  with any speed deterrents near Sycamore School. Public Works Director DuBoux
  stated the Traffic Engineer had determined a speed hump could not be installed
  there.

  In response to Chair Frost, Ex Officio Member Woodworth listed the members of
  Congress involved in HR 176. He discussed aspects of the bill, including
  eliminating impacts on veterans benefit eligibility.

  Commissioner Gibbs asked if the traffic signal by McDonald’s and Nobu could be
  moved. Public Works Director DuBoux stated it was set up as a pedestrian signal
  and would be addressed in the PCH Signal Synchronization Project. He stated it
  would be upgraded to a full traffic signal and would be shifted slightly. He stated
  the Planning Commission was waiting for a Nobu coastal development permit
  (CDP). In response to Commissioner Gibbs, Public Works Director DuBoux stated
  the design was approved by Caltrans.

  Chair Frost discussed speeding in the west end of Malibu. He stated the word was
  out that there is no enforcement. He suggested deputies be there on Sunday
  mornings.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 6:52 p.m., Commissioner Gibbs moved and Chair Frost seconded a motion to
  adjourn. The question was called, and the motion carried 3-0, Vice Chair Spiegel
  and Commissioner Merrick absent.
